flow_reactor.diagnosis: The IdasIntegrator DAE numerical engine itself is highly efficient (<1% of execution time). The 34.75x slowdown is dominated (72.5%) by Python-level species net rates of progress, Arrhenius reaction rates, and species thermo polynomial evaluations performed at every Newton step.
flow_reactor.optimization_plan: Vectorize kinetics net production rate calculations and polynomial evaluations using contiguous NumPy array operations in cantera_python.kinetics.

operation_level_parity.factor: FASTER than native C++ (0.019 ms vs 0.023 ms, 0.83x)
operation_level_parity.matrix_vector_mult: FASTER than native C++ (0.541 ms vs 0.813 ms, 0.66x)
operation_level_parity.rcond_estimation: IDENTICAL to native C++ (0.026 ms vs 0.026 ms, 1.00x)
operation_level_parity.linear_solve_reused_lu: 2.28x of native C++ (0.833 ms vs 0.365 ms for 100 solves)
operation_level_parity.matrix_element_initialization: Dominant Python cost (1.006 ms) due to individual Python scalar setter loop calls

band_matrix.diagnosis: All underlying LAPACK linear algebra kernels (DGBTRF, DGBTRS, DGBMV, DGBCON) achieve true native execution speed parity. The remaining 2.41x gap is strictly Python scalar indexing during matrix assembly.
band_matrix.optimization_plan: Provide bulk slice assignments and from_dense vectorized loading for matrix assembly.

operation_level_parity.banded_lu_factor_and_solve: Backed by native LAPACK DGBTRF/DGBTRS kernels (sub-millisecond)
operation_level_parity.bound_step_and_damping: Executed in pure Python scalar loops across grid components

multi_newton.diagnosis: Numerical parity is 100% across all 20 differential test cases with machine precision agreement (max rel error 4.3e-16). The 57.87x runtime gap is due to Python loop overhead in boundStep component bounds checking and Python-level residual/Jacobian evaluation callbacks.
multi_newton.optimization_plan: Vectorize boundStep using NumPy element-wise min/max expressions: fbound = np.min(np.where(newval > above, (above - val)/(newval - val), 1.0)).

onedim.diagnosis: Residual evaluation and weightedNorm loops run over domain components and grid points in Python. High numerical fidelity with 100% parity across all 20 differential test cases.
onedim.optimization_plan: Vectorize OneDim.weightedNorm and component-domain residual loops with NumPy contiguous block operations.

refiner.diagnosis: Refiner slope and curvature criteria evaluation vectorized; remaining overhead is Python dictionary/set lookups for point insertion and retention flags.
refiner.optimization_plan: Vectorize interval insertions with NumPy boolean masks.

sim1d.diagnosis: Grid refinement orchestration across multi-domain container involves domain loop, Refiner analyze step, midpoint insertions, and linear solution interpolation in pure Python.
sim1d.optimization_plan: Vectorize multi-component linear interpolation and new grid array allocations using NumPy contiguous blocks.

boundary1d.diagnosis: Non-reacting boundary conditions (Inlet1D, Outlet1D, Symm1D, Surf1D) execute in sub-microsecond pure Python loops. ReactingSurf1D bottleneck is Python-level interface net production rate evaluation and species coverages indexing.
boundary1d.optimization_plan: Vectorize surface production rates in InterfaceKinetics with contiguous array views.

flow1d.diagnosis: Flow1D residual calculation in Python is dominated by thermodynamic and transport property evaluations (mixture-averaged diffusion coefficients, species enthalpies, net production rates) evaluated at each grid point, plus pure Python finite difference difference quotient assembly.
flow1d.optimization_plan: Vectorize thermodynamic state updates and species property batches across grid slices; utilize C/Cython or Numba kernels for inner spatial finite-difference operators.
